about: Eight ground-floor rooms of 1897 from Magic's catalogue (reqs 2473 and 2478): the duelling practice room, the visitors' parlour, the post room, the staff dining room, the Gobstones Club's room, the old music room, the Keeper's Key Room (the old lodge) and the Quidditch kit room. The visitors' fire waits on Story (req 2474) and the squirt's softening on Story and Godric (req 2480, 2483); both marked.

show: pairs of pupils at the club's practice, wands in hand, facing one another along the chalked floor; an ordinary evening's practice
room.canon: Magic's req 2473 (docs/magic/rooms.md, Three ground-floor rooms the catalogue lacked, 1897): an ordinary practice evening (world rules, Classes; never CoS 11's night); the spells are the lesson's, never this table's; the club's evening stands for hour 19 to 22, ours

show: the room empty and still, the gauntlets on the plank bench, no mark on the wall, nothing left that tells what was done
room.canon: Magic's req 2473 (docs/magic/rooms.md, Three ground-floor rooms the catalogue lacked, 1897): after the club and before it, outside the club's night: empty, unmarked; ours

show: the room empty and still, the gauntlets on the plank bench, no mark on the wall, nothing left that tells what was done
room.canon: Magic's req 2473 (docs/magic/rooms.md, Three ground-floor rooms the catalogue lacked, 1897): after the club: empty, unmarked; ours

show: the fire banked low in the grate, the room cool, nobody there to be waited on; a pamphlet and a teacup on the pedestal table
room.canon: Magic's req 2473 (docs/magic/rooms.md, Three ground-floor rooms the catalogue lacked, 1897): quiet and banked, the pamphlet and teacup as Interiors has them (docs/interiors/ground-floor-lived-in-1029.md)

show: the morning's letters sliding one by one out of the sack and into the pigeonholes, each to its own slot, the overstuffed slot taking one more than it should and holding
room.canon: Magic's req 2473 (docs/magic/rooms.md, Three ground-floor rooms the catalogue lacked, 1897): the letters the owls leave here rather than at the table ("about a hundred owls", PS 8 L2754, read in the canon tool, 1 November 2026); the sorting is the post's housekeeping, ours; the hours stand for after breakfast

show: the pigeonholes colour-coded by how fast a letter is wanted, a letter staying in its colour and gone by next morning
room.canon: Magic's req 2473 (docs/magic/rooms.md, Three ground-floor rooms the catalogue lacked, 1897): "colour-coded depending on how fast you want your letter to get there" (B3 ch8 L16466, the village's own way, an everyday thing a later book names first and this room may keep)

show: the supper laid on the golden plates as the door is opened, the dishes there and no one yet in; a boy who walks in is not served
room.canon: Magic's req 2478 (docs/magic/rooms.md, Five more ground-floor rooms of 1897): "the feast appeared suddenly on the golden plates" (PS 10 L3536, the Hall's own way, here for the few places a master takes); ours for the room; the boys' tables are the Hall's and the kitchens'; meal = dinner is the evening meal, 18.30

show: the plates wiped clean and the cloth bare, the one pulled-out chair left as it was
room.canon: Magic's req 2478 (docs/magic/rooms.md, Five more ground-floor rooms of 1897): "wiped clean" (GoF 16 L26713, a later book's everyday thing, which may stand in every year); the chair is Interiors'

show: a bare table, the chairs in, nothing laid; the kettle is the staff room's
room.canon: Magic's req 2478 (docs/magic/rooms.md, Five more ground-floor rooms of 1897): otherwise: bare

show: a bare table, the chairs in, nothing laid; the kettle is the staff room's
room.canon: Magic's req 2478 (docs/magic/rooms.md, Five more ground-floor rooms of 1897): otherwise: bare

show: a game going in the chalk rings, the stones rolled; a point lost and a stone squirts a nasty-smelling liquid across a player's cuff, never his face, and he laughs as the club hands him the cloth; every regular's cuff is stained, and the stain is the club's badge
room.canon: Magic's req 2478, amended by req 2557 (settled 217, Godric, 1 November 2026, 12.51 pm; docs/magic/rooms.md, the Gobstones Club's room): "squirt a nasty-smelling liquid" (PA 4 L14230, read in the canon tool, 1 November 2026); a lost point lands on the cuff, never the face (FDP-11), the club hands him the cloth; every regular has a stained cuff, so a boy who gets one is told he has the club's mark; the club plays the brothers as a pair against a pair, never brother against brother, so a stained cuff is shared and nothing ranks one over the other

show: one old set in the cabinet with a stone missing, the stone lying loose in the corner
room.canon: Magic's req 2478 (docs/magic/rooms.md, Five more ground-floor rooms of 1897): "an old set of Gobstones" (GoF 20 L28353) and "old Gobstones" (OotP 14 L41614), a later book's everyday thing that may stand in every year; ours for the room

show: the board of past captains in gilt, strangers all, not a name the boys know
room.canon: Magic's req 2478 (docs/magic/rooms.md, Five more ground-floor rooms of 1897): strangers all (Story), none from a later book's years; the captain's photograph (HBP 25 L63954) is held for the books' years and is not hung; the name is never read aloud to a boy (FDP-37); the names are Story's (req 2480)

show: a board of past captains on the wall, a dozen Scottish surnames in gilt down the forty years to now, each with a small brown thumb-smudge beside it, the last line this year's captain; strangers all, seen and never read aloud, nothing on it to tap
room.canon: Magic's req 2593, from Story's settled 219 (Godric, 1 November 2026, 1.43 pm, his 1 on req 2555; docs/magic/rooms.md, the Gobstones Club's room, the board of captains): a dozen Scottish surnames (Ferrier, Tulloch, Lorimer, Menzies and so on, in none of the seven books, by Story's search), the stained-cuff badge of settled 217 carried onto the board as a thumb-smudge; nobody on it is anyone the boys know, no name from a later book hangs there; a captain's photograph (HBP 25 L63954) is held for the books' years and not hung; the name is never read aloud to a boy (FDP-37); a thing seen, not tapped

show: the school song's sheet on the square piano's stand, words only, no notes; a cupboard of school instruments by the wall
room.canon: Magic's req 2478 (docs/magic/rooms.md, Five more ground-floor rooms of 1897): "everyone pick their favorite tune" (PS 7 L2617): a boy who sings it picks his own, and the room does not correct it; ours for the stand

show: each key hanging under its door's brass tag on the board; a key a master borrowed is not back yet
room.canon: Magic's req 2478 (docs/magic/rooms.md, Five more ground-floor rooms of 1897): the board of keys; the room is Mrs. Wardlaw's (settled 203); ours

show: every key back on its hook under its brass tag, no hand having hung them, the doors they open locked again
room.canon: Magic's req 2478 (docs/magic/rooms.md, Five more ground-floor rooms of 1897): a key a master has borrowed is back on its hook by the evening bell with no hand to hang it, the door locked again as alohomora-1897.md (rule 5) has locks lock; ours

show: a strapped ball chest by the wall
room.canon: Magic's req 2478 (docs/magic/rooms.md, Five more ground-floor rooms of 1897): the chest strapped shut ("the three balls left inside the box", PS 10 L3456)

show: a jumper and a scarf hung on the airer, dry within the hour
room.canon: Magic's req 2478 (docs/magic/rooms.md, Five more ground-floor rooms of 1897): "Professor Flitwick had dried himself off with a wave of his wand" (HBP 17 L60868, a later book's everyday thing that may stand in every year); the airer is Interiors'

show: a charm goes wide and a stream of red and gold sparks spills out of a wand's end, throwing dancing spots of light on the stone, drifting along it and going out; the wall is as it was
records.canon: Magic's req 2473 (docs/magic/rooms.md, Three ground-floor rooms the catalogue lacked, 1897): "a stream of red and gold sparks ... throwing dancing spots of light on to the walls" (PS 5 L1649, a wand's sparks, read in the canon tool, 1 November 2026); the sparks fade on their own, no rule drinks them; nothing is struck, nothing is harmed

show: a grown-up visitor she knows is shown in by the Keeper of Keys, who clicks her fingers; a fire bursts into life in the grate, and she goes, saying nothing
records.canon: Settled 216 (Godric, 1 November 2026, 12.51 pm; docs/story/settled.md; Magic's req 2557, docs/magic/rooms.md, the visitors' parlour): the Keeper's click of her fingers (B3 ch3 L14089, the Leaky Cauldron's parlour, an everyday wizard's way with a fire, read in the canon tool, 1 November 2026); no words in either case

show: a grown-up visitor she does not know is shown in; the Keeper of Keys lays a taper to the grate by hand, slowly, and the room stays banked a little longer; she says nothing, and goes
records.canon: Settled 216 (Godric, 1 November 2026, 12.51 pm; Magic's req 2557): a stranger gets a taper laid by hand, slowly, the room banked a little longer than the click's, no words, so a boy can tell whom she trusts without being told; the taper's flame is its own

show: a letter for him among the day's, in the slot of his house, and he takes it down
records.canon: Magic's req 2473 (docs/magic/rooms.md, Three ground-floor rooms the catalogue lacked, 1897): a boy's own letter now and then, taken by his hand; Howlers are the brother-post's and not this room's, and the owl post between the boys (B26) is the owls' own and not routed through here; what it says is the boy's and private (FDP-25)
Magic's req 2473 (docs/magic/rooms.md, Three ground-floor rooms the catalogue lacked, 1897): the other half of the draw: no letter this time

show: he takes one out, and it sounds a little truer in his hands than it should; the square piano stays out of tune
records.canon: Magic's req 2478 (docs/magic/rooms.md, Five more ground-floor rooms of 1897): ours: as a piano out of tune never is for long to a child who is trying; nothing lights, nothing is marked

show: a bell on the board rings and its numbered flag drops for the room that called; a while later the flag rights itself, the Keeper having been
records.canon: Magic's req 2478 (docs/magic/rooms.md, Five more ground-floor rooms of 1897): a master or a prefect calls; ours, an 1897 household thing; the board is Mrs. Wardlaw's (settled 222, req 2614)

show: the pull gives, and far off a bell rings; on the Key Room's board that room's numbered flag drops
the ring of keys sounds first, then Mrs. Wardlaw at the door with a biscuit in her pocket: 'Rang for me? Then you will want tea.'
records.canon: Magic's req 2614 (settled 222, Godric, 1 November 2026, 2.03 pm; docs/magic/rooms.md, Mrs. Wardlaw's Key Room, the bell board): any room's bell-pull, ours; the ring sounds before she is seen (sound-day.md single drop); no scolding, no count of rings, nothing ranks a boy; the tea is the visitors' parlour's (settled 216). Bell-pull tap ids wait on the pages

show: her ring of keys jingling nearby, heard before she is seen
records.canon: Magic's req 2478 (docs/magic/rooms.md, Five more ground-floor rooms of 1897): the Keeper's ring at her belt (settled 203); the sound is the sound schedule's single drop (docs/magic/sound-day.md), this cue is the line a boy would read

show: a dull knock from inside the strapped chest, the lid lifting a finger's width and settling, a Bludger testing it
records.canon: Magic's req 2478 (docs/magic/rooms.md, Five more ground-floor rooms of 1897): the ordinary two, never aimed at anyone; the rogue one of CoS 10 L10025 is the book's and is not used; ours for the knock
